annotations.title: Pre-flight check of a programmable token transfer

description: Would a transfer of a programmable token (CIP-113) from A to B be allowed, and if not, why? Answers only from state we index (the sender's balance under the standard's contract, a pause or shutdown, the block list of either side) and lists what it can NOT know: identity checks signed off chain, the issuer's own transfer script, a rule change before the transaction is built. The best verdict is `nothing_visible_forbids`, never "allowed". A token whose rules are scripts we cannot read answers `rules_unreadable`. Nothing is built or signed.

amount.description: Amount to send, decimal-adjusted, as plain digits (for example "10" or "2.5").

from.description: Sender: addr1… address (ordinary or smart-wallet), stake1… address or a 56-hex owner credential.

to.description: Receiver: addr1… address (ordinary or smart-wallet), stake1… address or a 56-hex owner credential.

unit.description: Token unit: policy id + asset name in hex.
